messages.subject: gpcount data formatting
parts:
Hi All,
I am struggling to get my data into a format useable in gpcount:  I have a long-format data frame that look like this for each species,

point_ID_2 occasion wind wet temp_anomaly month decimal_start season distance time_step3
187  AU10A1       1    4   3   -0.3925972    10          6.17      1      150          2
190  AU10A1       1    0   1   -2.3925972     4          6.38      2      142          2
188  AU10A1       1    0   2    1.1074028     3          6.32      2      150          1
191  AU10A1       1    0   2    3.1074028    10          6.78      1      160          1
194  AU10A1       1    3   1   -5.8925972     6          8.08      1      148          2
193  AU10A1       1    0   1    4.6074028     2          8.83      2      165          1
    year     count
187    1997     1
190    1997     1
188    2004     0
191    1998     0
194    1998     1
193    1998     1

with repeat surveys at sites within years, seasons, and one of two time-steps.  I am thinking to use year-season combinations as my secondary periods and time-step as my primary, but my survey design is unbalanced (so that not all sites have surveys in all combinations of year, season and time-step) I have so far been unable to work out a way (using e.g. reshape) to get this into a wide format populated with the necessary NA values for missing surveys in the design.  Any tips or helper functions would be much appreciated!
Cheers
A

messages.author: 527d9b3ec7deff2d
messages.subject: Re: gpcount data formatting
parts:
If you know how to use the reshape package to melt and cast your data frame, create a new column called "sampled" and set that to 1 for each record.  Then use melt and cast to create a matrix where the measured variable (measure.var) = "sampled" and set all zeros to NA.  Now when you create a matrix of the counts, you multiply it by the "sampled" matrix (which should be 1s and NAs).

data$sampled <- 1
data.melt1 <- melt(data, id.var=c("site","survey"), measure.var="sampled")
sample.matrix <- cast(data.melt1, site ~ survey)
sample.matrix[sample.matrix==0] <- NA

data.melt2 <- melt(data, id.var=c("site","survey"), measure.var="count")
count.matrix <- cast(data.melt2, site ~ survey)

count.matrix <- count.matrix*sample.matrix
